findings.description: The `finally` clause runs after both the success and failure paths. On failure, `job.next_run` is set to `now + retry_delay` at line 65, then `finally` immediately overwrites it with `now + job.interval`. The backoff/retry_delay feature therefore never takes effect: failed jobs wait a full interval before retrying, contrary to the Job docstring.
findings.suggestion: Set `job.next_run = now + job.interval` only in the `else` branch (or before the try), and remove the `finally` block so the failure path keeps its retry delay.
findings.title: finally block overwrites the retry-delay next_run on failure

findings.description: `job.retry_delay * 2 ** (consecutive_failures - 1)` grows without bound if `max_failures` is large. Jobs are disabled at max_failures, but a very large max_failures (or a job whose count is set externally) can make the integer huge and `timedelta * int` raise OverflowError. That exception would escape `_run`'s except block and break the tick.
findings.suggestion: Cap the exponent, e.g. `2 ** min(job.consecutive_failures - 1, 20)`, or catch OverflowError and fall back to `job.interval`.
findings.title: Unbounded exponent in backoff computation
